newsitem.title: India: Indian shares end mixed, Bombay lower in kerb.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares end mixed, Bombay lower in kerb.

text.p: ** Indian shares end mixed after see-sawing wildly in a session driven by punters, traders say
** A sharp drop in first half net profits of India's largest cement maker ACC pulls its share price 11.8 percent lower in off-market kerb deals
** Bombay's benchmark stocks index closes 46.54 points or 1.55 percent down at 2948.44
** The 50-stocks index of National Stock Exchange (NSE) ends 3.26 points lower at 848.74
** Delhi shares end up but off session's highs
Indian shares ended mixed on Tuesday in a volatile session driven by punters, traders said.
Bombay's benchmark stocks index closed 46.54 points or 1.55 percent down at 2948.44.
Prices fell further in off-market kerb deals after the country's largest cement maker ACC announced a steep fall in first half net profit.

ACC shares slid 11.8 percent to 1,020 rupees in off-market kerb deals on Tuesday after the firm said its net fell 56 percent to 550.5 million rupees in the six months to September 30, 1996 from 1.25 billion rupees in the year-ago period.
Results fell sharply below market expectations of a net profit of around 900 million rupees. ACC said it could not recover an unprecedented hike in input cost which hit margins.
Traders said funds were cautious participants on the BSE.
"Funds were semi-active. Most of the action was driven by speculators," said a trader at a foreign brokerage.
Analyst Mehmood Khan at Times Guaranty Financial Ltd said the index was likely to form a new bottom at 2905-2865 levels.
Prices on the NSE shot past BSE levels on hectic squaring off on the last day of the account.
Auto firms TELCO, Bajaj Auto and Mahindra & Mahindra continued to head lower as some securities firms recommended investors underweight the sector on fears of a prolonged slowdown in the economy.
In Delhi, shares closed higher on fund buying but a bout of late profit-taking trimmed early gains, brokers said.
The Delhi sensitive index closed up 6.36 points at 669.14 after touching a day's high of 674.15.
"Huge short-covering at lower levels was the main reason for the rally in share prices," said Manoj Choraria of brokers Choraria Investments.
